name: The Comfort Maple

location.address: Comfort Maple Conservation Area, 636 Metler Rd, Fenwick (North Pelham), Ontario L0S 1C0, Canada

access: Free, year-round, sunrise to sunset. A small conservation area (a single-tree park, basically) run by the Niagara Peninsula Conservation Authority, with parking on site. No gate, no fee, no permission needed.
transport: Rural site off Metler Road near Fenwick/North Pelham; no transit stop nearby, reached by car. Roughly 1.5 hours' drive from Toronto or 20-25 minutes from St. Catharines/Welland.
verify_notes: Widely cited as the oldest sugar maple in Canada, and possibly the oldest of any species in Ontario. AGE: the Ontario Forestry Association estimated 400-500 years in 1975 and has separately floated a figure as high as 541, but Wikipedia is explicit this is NOT based on a full ring count (drilling a 500-year-old living tree's core is itself invasive and is not how this figure was reached) -- so treated here as a real but unusually wide estimate, kept broad (age_min 400, age_max 541) rather than picking one number. SIZE: height 24.4-24.5m (about 80 feet), trunk circumference at base 6m (20 feet, recorded as girth_cm 600), crown spread/circumference given as 38m (125 feet) by Wikipedia. HISTORY: on land held by the Comfort family from 1816 (145 years) until Edna Eleanor Comfort donated it to the Niagara Peninsula Conservation Authority on 1961-04-30; designated an Ontario Heritage Act heritage tree in June 2000. CONDITION, the honest complication: the tree has taken at least one major lightning strike and has visible old repairs (brick and concrete fill in trunk wounds, guy wires supporting branches). A certified-arborist report by Urban Forest Innovations Inc. (commissioned by NPCA, month/year not pinned down exactly from available sources but referenced as a recent assessment) found the tree in 'fair structural condition and health,' in 'a state of slow decline, consistent with the tree's advanced age,' and judged 'manageable for continued retention' with NPCA and contractors following its preservation recommendations. That is a tree in active professional stewardship, not one known to be dying or dead -- passes the alive-now bar, flagged because 'slow decline' should be said honestly on the page rather than glossed as pristine. DESTINATION TEST: passes clearly -- an entire small conservation area exists around this single tree, it carries a heritage designation in its own name, and it is the specific, named subject of regional news coverage about its condition, which is the behaviour of something people go and check on rather than an anonymous old tree in a park. CONTAINER: Fenwick/North Pelham is roughly 1.5 hours from Toronto (the only nearby published city, data/cities/toronto.json), well outside the 30-minute day-trip boundary, and it is not meaningfully close to any other published city. Recommend as its own single-tree place, 'Pelham' or 'Fenwick, Ontario', under the 2026-08-31 exception. PIN: coordinates from Wikipedia's infobox, matching the NPCA's own street address (636 Metler Rd) and describing the conservation area itself (a small dedicated park built around this one tree, not a large multi-feature park), so treated as confirmed rather than merely approximate.
